title: A bulk order's quote event dropped in the refactor, refuted on the route's trace of sends
summary: The value-object refactor of 190, with the route sending no `QuoteEvent` for an order of 100 items or more. The total is the same on every request, so every test of the answer passes. The tool compares the ordered trace of the route's sends and refutes it on a 100-item order, the witness replayed on the JVM under recording stubs.

change.description: `Quote`'s amount, a `long` of cents, becomes a value object, `Money`, so `Quote(long cents, int quantity)` is now `Quote(Money amount, int quantity)`; `Pricing.total` reads `q.amount.cents()` where it read `q.cents`; the pure helper `Pricing.discount` (a tenth off ten items or more) is rewritten as an early return; and the route `POST /quotes` makes the quote with `new Money(cents)`. Nothing is meant to change: not the total, not the event the route sends, not what `Pricing.withQuantity` hands back. In this version the route also sends the event only when `quantity < 100`.

risk: A rewrite of the glue around a kernel can lose a send for a case nobody tests, and nothing the route returns shows it: the consumer of the `quotes` topic just never hears of the order.
explanation: The route's observation spec makes each `KafkaTemplate.send` an observation, with the payload paths a consumer reads (`data.total`, `data.quantity`) snapshotted at the call. Both builds' sends are replaced by the same recording stub, and the tool's own checker proves or refutes that the two logs are equal, in exact order. On a quote of 100 items with a positive total, the old build attempts one send and the new one none.
resolution: Send the event for every positive total, as before.
notes: Checked by `jvmcontract compare`, which build.py runs as the B9 check of the shop app (`run_tool_compare`): the unpatched build against the patched one, twice under one fresh proof cache, the verdict read from the rerun and the page's output from the first run. The verdict is the subject's; the page lists every other part the run checked.

The joint example of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md`'s Phase 5, made an example: the app's sources are the fixture's `before` build (`lib/tests/fixtures/foundations/`), and the patch turns them into its `after` build with the dropped-effect defect (`defects/dropped-effect/`) overlaid. `lib/tests/compare.rs` holds `jvmcontract compare` to the same builds inline; this is the same run by build.py, with the app's tests run too.

Nothing in the run is written by hand. The entry points' external inputs (`cents`, `quantity`) are anchored by their observation specs, so no mapping is involved at the boundary. The kernel's relation between the old and new quotes (`old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents`, `old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity`) is alignment's proposal, inferred from how the two constructors route their parameters into the fields; it stays *proposed*, its evidence the proof under its claim key, and since nothing external anchors a kernel method's inputs, a proved relation there is reported as proved and not as the intended one.

What stays unresolved in every example of the set, by name: `POST /quotes/text` (its string concatenation isn't modeled), `Quote#cents` moved to `Money#cents` (a method of a class the old build doesn't have) and the instance method `Quote#quantity` (the regression check takes static methods, or a record's over its primitive components).

Run inline on 2026-11-07 (JDK 25.0.5), `jvmcontract compare` on the app compiled unpatched and patched, as build.py compiles it, and on the fixture's builds, with the same verdicts (the times are the fixture's): `POST /quotes` refuted, replayed on a JVM under the recording stubs; the kernel's `total`, `withQuantity` and `discount` verified. 0.4 s cold, 0.2 s warm.
The app's tests pass on this version: none sends 100 items.
provenance: Constructed for Phase 5 of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md` (the joint example, made an example under the numbers 190-199). Examples 190 to 196 share the refactor: 190 is the refactor alone, and 191 to 196 each add one of the fixture's defects to it.

references.title: Godlin and Strichman, Regression verification: proving the equivalence of similar programs (2013)
Barthe, Crespo and Kunz, Relational verification using product programs (2011)
